_comment: Budgets for `npm run audit:perf`. A tripwire against regression, not a
target: every number sits deliberately ABOVE the measurement taken when
it was written, so an ordinary change never trips it and a doubling does.
THE NUMBERS HERE ARE UNCOMPRESSED, because that is what the tool sees.
`encodedBodySize` on a local `node app.cjs` is the raw body — the host
gzips, measured 2026-09-21: the home document is 348 KB raw and 76 KB on
the wire. So `documentKb` and `totalKb` are a proxy for how much the page
asks the browser to parse, not for what a visitor downloads.
Baseline, local release build, 390px / CPU x4 / cache off:
LCP median 1140 ms, document 342 KB, JS decoded 418 KB, total 1007 KB.
Live for comparison: LCP median 628 ms, TTFB 153 ms, CLS 0.
The local LCP spread is wide (584-1652) — a cold Node process answering
its first requests. Compare local against local, never local against live.
`lcpElement` is the load-bearing entry. The hero headline losing that
place is how the cookie notice became the LCP element at 4.1 s, and no
byte count would have shown it.
Devices (2026-09-21): mobile 390px and desktop 1440px. Each may carry its
own lcpElement and budget overrides under devices.<name>. The desktop is
where the hero photo loads and Motion is busiest; the H1 has to stay the
LCP element there too, or a start state has overtaken it.
